scope: Two contained private3102 development Webpack sampling profiles; ten read-only routes, same current-source snapshot, normal Console authentication, no jobs. No public process or source configuration changed.
mainProfileMissingExplanation: Installed Next CLI defaults to100ms before SIGKILL during shutdown; second run sets private-only NEXT_EXIT_TIMEOUT_MS=30000 and allows up to40s for its owned group to exit. This diagnoses collection, not a public-runtime fix.
findings: Second main-server sampled live allocations total approximately5.0GiB at shutdown, including1196MiB readFileSync and507.1MiB Map.set under Webpack process calls. These are allocation stacks, not object-retainer paths.
Aggregate sampled process RSS peaks7.31 and7.44GiB, with no threshold restart in either bounded workload. Sampling adds overhead; RSS includes native and multiple child processes.

Next installed webpack-config already sets dev maxMemoryGenerations=0; webpackMemoryOptimizations already enabled. No unsupported cache override, heap increase or default compiler change is justified.
limitations: Single workload twice is diagnostic, not browser readiness,20-navigation/50-API or p95 acceptance.
Profiles are saved during shutdown and may reflect cleanup/GC; not the peak retained heap.
Not every process emitted a profile. First run lacks main compiler profile, so its worker profiles cannot classify compiler retention.
Shared machine and database activity remain confounders; no memory leak or long-session stability claim.
